html:
Chinghiz Aitmatov was a Kyrgyz novelist and the best known writer of Soviet Central Asia. He wrote mostly in Russian, also in Kyrgyz, and his books were translated into over a hundred languages.

He grew up in a village in Kyrgyzstan. His father, a Communist official, was shot in the Great Purge of 1938. Aitmatov studied animal husbandry and worked on farms before he began to write.

His short novel Jamila (1958), the love story of a village woman during the Second World War, made him famous; the French poet Louis Aragon called it the most beautiful love story in the world. Other books include Farewell, Gulsary! and The White Ship. In The Day Lasts More Than a Hundred Years (1980) a railway worker on the steppe lives beside a space launch site like Baikonur. It retells the legend of the mankurt, a slave robbed of his memory, an image of people cut off from their past.

Under Gorbachev he was a voice for reform, and later an ambassador for Kyrgyzstan in Europe.
